query: how to make an ai agent ask before it acts
title: How to make an AI agent ask before it acts | 50agents
description: Make an AI agent ask before it acts: sort actions by risk, hold risky ones in an approval the software enforces, show the full action, plan for silence.
h1: How to make an AI agent ask before it acts
answer: Sort every action the AI agent can take into "does alone" and "asks first", put sends, payments, deletions and access changes in the second group, and use a tool that holds those until a person approves them.
Each approval should show exactly what will happen, let you change it, and stay open until someone answers.

sections.h2: Why "ask me first" in the prompt is not enough

body.p: You can tell a model to check with you before doing anything risky, and it usually will. Anthropic publishes exactly such a prompt, then says plainly that prompt text guides the model but enforces nothing; for anything that moves money, a person should approve each call in the software. OWASP lists human approval of high-impact actions as a defence against AI agents doing too much.
The test: if the AI agent decided to skip the question, would the action still go through? If yes, you have a polite request, not an approval.

head: Group
Examples
What happens
rows: Reading email, searching a CRM, reading a web page, writing a note in its own report
Runs, and shows up in its log.
Sending an email or message to anyone else, changing a record in your apps
Waits for a yes, with the full action shown.
Payments and refunds, deleting, sharing files, adding people or changing access
Waits for a yes, no matter what you loosen elsewhere.

body.p: OpenAI’s builder guide suggests the same sort: rate each tool low, medium or high by whether it only reads, whether it can be undone, and how much money is involved, and hand control to a person on high-risk actions and when the AI agent keeps failing.

ul: **Who is asking and from where:** which AI agent, on which run.
**Exactly what will happen:** the recipient, the subject and the full text; the record and the field and the new value; the amount and who gets it.
**Why:** one line of the AI agent’s reasoning, so you can spot a wrong premise.
**Change, not only yes or no:** most approvals need a small edit, and a reviewer who can only decline will approve things they should have fixed.
**It stays open:** an unanswered approval should wait, not expire into "yes".

method.h2: How to set it up, step by step

steps.title: List every action the AI agent can take
steps.body: From its apps: read, create, update, send, delete, share. You will be surprised how many it has.

steps.title: Put each one in a group
steps.body: Use the table above. When in doubt, put it in asks first; you can move it later.

steps.title: Remove what it never needs
steps.body: An action it never uses should not be there at all. Fewer actions means fewer approvals and less to go wrong.

steps.title: Pick where approvals arrive
steps.body: One place you check a few times a day, on your phone too. Approvals scattered across email, chat and dashboards get missed.

steps.title: Watch the approve-without-edits rate
steps.body: If you approve almost everything of one kind unchanged for a few weeks, consider letting that kind run alone. If you edit most, fix the instructions.

steps.title: Plan for retries
steps.body: An approved action can run twice if the tool crashes in between. OpenAI’s SDK docs advise making approved actions safe to repeat; ask your tool how it handles this.

example.h2: How it works in 50agents: Needs you
body: 50agents puts every approval in one place called Needs you, on its own screen, on Home and in the chat it came from. By default anything that spends money, reaches people outside your workspace or changes access asks first, and you set each AI agent’s freedom from there. An item stays open until you tap an answer; the AI agent never answers it for you.

wrong.title: Rubber-stamping
wrong.body: Too many approvals and you stop reading them. Trim what asks, and group low-risk items into one daily report instead.

wrong.title: Approving without context
wrong.body: The card says "Send email?" without the text. Never approve what you cannot see in full.

wrong.title: Nobody answers
wrong.body: The approval sits for a week and the moment passes. Check approvals at fixed times, and give the AI agent a rule for stale items ("if not approved in 2 days, drop it and tell me").

wrong.title: The AI agent decides when to ask
wrong.body: If asking is up to the AI, one day it will not ask. Put the rule in the tool’s settings, not only in the prompt.

wrong.title: Approved twice
wrong.body: A retry after a crash sends the same email again. Prefer tools that record each approved action once.

faqs.q: What is human in the loop for AI agents?
faqs.a: A person approves certain actions before they happen. It is different from a person reviewing a report after the fact, which some call human on the loop.

faqs.q: Can I approve from my phone?
faqs.a: Pick a tool where you can. Approvals that wait for you to be at a desk slow the AI agent down to your desk hours.

faqs.q: When can I let it act without asking?
faqs.a: When you have approved that kind of action unchanged many times, and a mistake would be cheap and easy to undo. Never for payments, deletions or access.
